name: ticket-desk
title: Ticket desk
summary: Route 3,000 support tickets to eight queues and flag the urgent ones while the words change.

brief.goal: You are a support desk's router. One ticket arrives each turn, 3,000 in all: its text as word ids, and what the desk knows about the customer. Send it to one of eight queues and say whether it is a P1 (urgent). You have 150 P1 flags. The words are in the release file `vocab.txt`. Between turns 1,000 and 2,200 new product names and error strings appear; on some seeds one queue's words change too, or what counts as a P1 shifts. The truth comes two turns later, in `feedback`.
brief.scoring: Out of 100, over resolved tickets. **Routing, 55:** 55 × the mean credit: 1 for the right queue, ½ for an adjacent one (3 to 5 pairs a seed, not shown), ¼ for `general`, 0 for any other. **P1, 25:** 15 × the share of true P1s you flagged, plus 10 × the share of the desk's flags that were on P1s. **Change, 20:** 20 × accuracy after the change ÷ max(accuracy before it, 0.3), capped at 20; 0 if the match ends early.
brief.ending: After 3,000 tickets (completed). Early, as a failure, when you have asked for more than 450 P1s (p1-storm), or when the mean credit of the last 300 resolved tickets falls below ¼, what sending everything to `general` earns (collapse).
brief.reward: Each turn: the change in score as a ticket resolves, plus 0.02 for a P1 you flagged and minus 0.02 for one you missed. The extras are taken back on the last turn, so the rewards add up to the score.

inputs.name: tokens
inputs.doc:
The ticket's text as 128 word ids, in reading order: the subject line, then the body, then 0s after the text ends.

Id n is the word on line n of the release file `vocab.txt` (4,095 lines of lowercase letters, line 1 is id 1), which comes with the practice files. To turn a text into ids, split it on spaces and replace each word by its line number. The words are made up: what they mean is learnt from the tickets.

The ids are laid out in groups, the same on every seed:

| Ids | Group |
|---|---|
| 1–360 | support wording every queue uses |
| 361–400 | urgency, outage and security markers |
| 401–2320 | the queues' own words: queue q (as in `queue`) owns 401 + 240q to 640 + 240q |
| 2321–3200 | product names and error strings that appear only after the change |
| 3201–4095 | filler; 3701–3900 are order ids and 3901–4095 error codes |

Each seed gives a queue 60 to 120 of its 240 ids and lends some of them to a similar queue, so a word's block is a strong hint, not the answer. About 0 to 10% of words are typos: an id moved 1 to 3 places.

inputs.name: ticket
inputs.doc: What the desk knows about the ticket before anyone reads it.

slices.name: age
slices.doc: How long the ticket has waited.

slices.name: has_error_code
slices.doc: 1 if the text has an error code (ids 3901–4095), else 0.

slices.name: has_order_id
slices.doc: 1 if the text has an order id (ids 3701–3900), else 0.

slices.name: prior_tickets
slices.doc: This customer's tickets in the last 30 days.

slices.name: reopened
slices.doc: 1 if it reopens a closed ticket, else 0.

slices.name: sentiment
slices.doc: The desk's mood score of the text: −1 angry to 1 happy.

slices.name: length
slices.doc: Words in the text: the ids in `tokens` that are not 0.

slices.name: hour
slices.doc: Local hour of day when it arrived.

slices.name: weekend
slices.doc: 1 on a Saturday or Sunday, else 0.

inputs.name: p1_flags_left
inputs.doc: P1 flags the desk can still raise for you. A request with none left still routes the ticket, at normal priority.

inputs.name: progress
inputs.doc: Share of the match played: 0 at the first ticket, 0.9997 at the last.

inputs.name: feedback
inputs.doc: The truth about the ticket you routed two turns ago, now that a person has picked it up. On the first two turns there is none: all zeros, with `valid` 0.

slices.name: queue
slices.doc: The queue you sent it to.

slices.name: was_p1
slices.doc: 1 if it was a P1, else 0.

slices.name: valid
slices.doc: 1 for a real result, 0 when there is none.

outputs.name: queue
outputs.doc: Where to send this turn's ticket.

codes.label: general
codes.doc: The holding queue. Only 4–10% of tickets belong here; any other ticket earns ¼.

outputs.name: p1
outputs.doc: 1 asks the desk to raise a P1 flag on this ticket, 0 is normal priority. The desk raises the first 150 requests; later ones still route the ticket at normal priority, and more than 450 requests end the match.

no_action: Send the ticket to `general` at normal priority: a quarter of a point at worst, never a P1 request.

stats.label: Score
stats.doc: The three terms in Scoring, added.

stats.label: Routing accuracy
stats.doc: Share of resolved tickets sent to exactly the right queue.

stats.label: P1 recall
stats.doc: Share of the true P1s the desk flagged for you.

stats.label: P1 precision
stats.doc: Share of the flags the desk raised that were on true P1s.

stats.label: Sent to general
stats.doc: Share of resolved tickets you sent to `general`: doubt when it is low, a habit when it is not.

stats.label: Accuracy before the change
stats.doc: Routing accuracy on the tickets that arrived before the change.

stats.label: Accuracy after the change
stats.doc: Routing accuracy on the tickets that arrived from the change on; 0 if the match ended before it.

stats.label: Recovery after the change
stats.doc: Turns from the change until accuracy over the last 200 resolved tickets came back within 0.05 of what it was at the change, counted once 200 tickets from after it had resolved. 3,000 when it never did.

endings.label: P1 storm
endings.doc: More than 450 P1 requests: three times the 150 flags.

endings.label: Routing collapse
endings.doc: The mean credit of the last 300 resolved tickets fell below ¼, what sending everything to `general` earns.

facts.label: Change
facts.doc: The turn whose ticket is the first one from after the change.

facts.label: What changed
facts.doc: What the change did besides bringing new product names.

codes.label: a queue's words
codes.doc: One queue lost 30–60% of its words to new ones.

codes.label: the P1 rule
codes.doc: What counts as a P1 shifted.

codes.label: both
codes.doc: A queue's words and the P1 rule.

facts.label: P1 share
facts.doc: Share of the match's tickets that were P1s.

facts.label: Typo rate
facts.doc: Share of words replaced by a nearby id.

facts.label: Adjacent queues
facts.doc: Which queue pairs earned half credit, as bits added: bit k is the k-th pair (i, j), i < j, in the order (0, 1), (0, 2) … (6, 7).

facts.label: Borrowed words
facts.doc: How much of a queue's words came from its similar queue, as a share of its own: the seed's routing difficulty.

facts.label: Tickets with new words
facts.doc: Share of the tickets from after the change with at least one new product name or error string.

series.label: Accuracy, last 200
series.doc: Routing accuracy over the last 200 resolved tickets. No sample until one has resolved.

series.label: P1 recall so far
series.doc: Share of the true P1s resolved so far that were flagged. No sample until one has resolved.

series.label: P1 flags left
series.doc: Flags the desk can still raise.

series.label: Tickets with new words
series.doc: Share of the tickets from after the change so far with a new product name or error string; 0 before the change.

events.label: New words
events.doc: New product names and error strings started to appear.

events.label: A queue's words changed
events.doc: One queue's words changed at the change.

events.label: P1 rule shifted
events.doc: What counts as a P1 shifted at the change.

events.label: P1 missed
events.doc: A true P1 resolved without a flag.
